I often find myself liking games that are part of a renowned series, but rejected by fans of said series because it is radically different.

For the purpose of the discussion, let's assume the games themselves are of great quality in either case. I understand that a sequel of Gran Turismo cannot be an FPS no matter how good it is, but a bad FPS would outright make the discussion irrelevant anyway.

Oftentimes, what is otherwise a good game gets a horrible press that just never clear out even though the game itself is solid and should please any fan of its (new) genre. Old fans just reject it, and non-fans miss out on it because they have no reason to check out the series, (especially the one episode that everyone hates).

In order not to keep it abstract, allow me to provide a few examples. They also include games that actually got good press, but that old-time fans tend to have rejected:

Sacred 3

  • To me it is a very solid Gauntlet-like game, almost to a T: trash mob genocide, A-to-B missions, get gold and XP then return to world map, excuse plot with forced jokes, extreme emphasis on empowering the player. In fact I like it a little more than Gauntlet because combat feedback is much more exaggerated, the game really wants you to feel that when you attack, it hurts. The thing is, this description is nothing at all like Sacred 1 and 2.

Ace Combat Assault Horizon

  • From Youtube videos I still don't really see how it is supposed to differ from the previous games. All I saw was a casual-friendly flight game with over-the-top action, essentially H.A.W.X with a more interesting gameplay gimmick (close-up dogfights!) and better story.

ArcaniA: A Gothic Tale

  • It used to be called Gothic 4, and indeed fans of the series (including me, as a major Gothic 2 & 3 fan) failed to see the kinship between the episodes, plus it didn't help that it suffered from numerous bugs near release. Now I only ever played the patched version: by the time I played it, the hate had dissipated and I had long forgotten any illusion of getting an actual "Gothic". What I got was a solid (although absolutely devoid of imagination or personality, almost to a comical level) action-RPG: good graphics, serviceable plot and lore, good controls with powerful combat feedback, in short never great but never bad either.

Guild Wars 2

  • It is so different from Guild Wars 1 that you could almost call it misleading advertising: the two games have nothing in common and liking one is zero indication that you are going to like the other. The only reason the title was kept was to ride the GW1 wave, something that the game, again, has no gameplay/technical legitimacy to do. Both games are largely beloved by critics and players alike, but there is still a serious amount of these people who like one and hate the other.

Long-running series are bound to evolve so I'm not going to name them all, but the Elder Scrolls, Fallout, Deux Ex, Thief, Rainbow Six, Ghost Recon, SimCity... All of these series have vastly different games, with significant numbers of fans and haters of both sides of the transformation.

How do you feel about these? Betrayal? Bad marketing? Necessary evolution? Would suggest them to people who disliked the old games but should (in theory) like the new?
Where do you stand on sequels that differ vastly from their origins?

Hard to tell, but in general, I think fans are forgiving (and even welcoming) if the sequel is good enough, but if it fails to achieve this subjective level, the fans will be merciless; even if the game is decent. (I think the problem has to do with niche genres with an obstinate fanbase rather than the games themselves)

Personally, I don't mind developers trying something new with known stuff, but I rather have them do it with spinoffs instead of the "main series". On the other hand, as you said, evolution is expected. But it's frequently made with the wrong mentality and we end with something that no one likes.

Both Sacred 3 and ArcaniA are sacrilege to respective franchises, ArcaniA in particular. It's like a big, steaming, slightly liquidy, putrid turd shat by an obese person on the legacy of Gothic franchise. Whoever authorized it should be shot.

I keep trying to think of games from the 80's and 90's that pulled it off. Ultima certainly did. But they also hammered out an Ultima game nearly every year. Between 1980 and 1994 they released 10 Ultima games. And a lot of changes were viewed as intrinsic improvements on Ultima's core philosophy. Origin's motto was "We Create Worlds" and Ultima constantly had game systems added which improved the feel of the world simulation. Then Ultima 8 added jumping and platforming and fans rebelled.

WIzardry ultimately floundered and failed because it was too stubborn about sticking to a formula. It wasn't until another designer took over with Wizardry V that the series began evolving somewhat. I remember loving the shit out of Wizardry 8 when it came out, and that was nothing at all like the other Wizardry games. Same thing goes for how much my mind was blown by Might & Magic VI. Huge departure from the rest of the series. Switched from grid based movement and turn based combat to free form movement with real time combat. And it was incredible.

I think in general you used to see sort of tick-tock cycle of evolutionary and revolutionary sequels. Fallout 1 to Fallout 2 was evolutionary. It took all the good parts of Fallout 1, made them better, while fixing the bad parts. Fallout 3 was revolutionary.

Fallout 4 devolved... however...

These days you see less revolutionary sequels, or even evolutionary sequels, and more devolving, cost cutting sequels. Oh they'll try to pass it off as "revolutionary". But we can all tell it's the same damned game we bought 5 years ago, except $20 more and with less content, simpler game mechanics, and a $20-50 season pass waiting in the wing.
